record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: For the double of a compact 4-manifold, a Kirby diagram of the double can be obtained by adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component of a Kirby diagram of the original manifold. Does the resulting 5-colored graph admit a standard modification procedure that produces ρ_3-pairs satisfying the hypotheses needed to construct a gem of the double?

evidence.quote: A particular case of this problem arises, for instance, in the construction of a gem for the double of a compact 4-manifold. It is known that a Kirby diagram of the double can be obtained, from a Kirby diagram of the manifold itself, by adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component (see [24]). Therefore, it may be worth investigating whether the particular configuration of the arising 5-colored graph allows to be modified in a standard way so as to give rise to ρ_3-pairs satisfying Proposition 9.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let M be a compact, connected, orientable PL 4-manifold with boundary, presented by a Kirby diagram K(M) (a framed link in S^3 describing the 1- and 2-handles attached to a 0-handle). The double DM := M ∪_{∂M} M is a closed orientable PL 4-manifold, and a Kirby diagram K(DM) of DM may be obtained from K(M) by adjoining, to each framed component of K(M), a 0-framed meridian (the standard "doubling" construction).

Let Γ(K(DM)) denote the 5-colored edge-coloured graph (with colour set {0,1,2,3,4}) associated to K(DM) by the standard procedure that translates a Kirby diagram of a closed 4-manifold into a 5-coloured graph (gem-candidate) representing a manifold PL-homeomorphic to DM. Within this framework one considers ρ_3-pairs: pairs of vertices in Γ joined by edges of three specified colours which, when satisfying suitable combinatorial hypotheses (the hypotheses required by the gem-construction proposition for closed 4-manifolds via ρ_3-pair cancellations), allow elementary moves that simplify Γ into a gem (a contracted, bipartite 5-coloured graph representing the manifold).

Question. Does the 5-coloured graph Γ(K(DM)) arising from the doubling Kirby diagram described above always admit a standard sequence of modifications producing ρ_3-pairs that satisfy the hypotheses needed for the gem-construction procedure, and hence yield a gem of the double DM directly from this combinatorial data?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open investigation in the survey on Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds. No subsequent work resolving the existence of the standard ρ_3-pair modification procedure for the doubling Kirby diagram appears in available sources.
